summary: mountainash-rules is built around two evaluation architectures (filter engine and accumulator engine) under core/ + engines/{filter,accumulator}/, sharing a dimension model, ternary logic system, and sentinel contract. Dependency direction is one-way: engines/accumulator -> engines/filter -> core; core never imports from engines/. Understanding the shared ternary invariant, the in-band set-wildcard sentinel, and the prime-product identity is key to confident maintenance across both engines.

concepts.name: Ternary logic encoding
concepts.description: The ternary invariant (1=match, 0=unknown, -1=non-match) is the foundation of evaluation correctness. Sentinels in constants.py map to ternary 0 through the mountainash t_col wrapper, and specificity is computed by counting only definite matches (1s). This invariant must hold across all 12 match strategies and all backends.

concepts.name: Sentinel contract
concepts.description: UNKNOWN/NOT_SET sentinels exist per data type: string ('<NA>'/'<NOT_SET>'), numeric (-999999999/-999999998), date/datetime (proleptic-floor dates). Bool dimensions use null as don't-care instead of a sentinel (no typed wildcard sentinel exists for bool). Set dimensions use an in-band '[sentinel]' list, never null.

concepts.name: Filter engine evaluation pipeline
concepts.description: evaluate() follows a 4-step pipeline: compile (DimensionCompiler at construction), bind (context -> __ctx_<dim> columns via context.py), evaluate (ternary columns + survival + specificity via _scored_relation, shared with explain()), select (sort/rank/hit-policy/cardinality via hit_policy.py). Each step is a pure DataFrame transformation.

concepts.name: Hit-policy selection layer
concepts.description: New since the prior profile: SelectionInfo carries what a RuleResult needs to re-apply policies post-hoc. check_assertions raises HitPolicyViolationError for UNIQUE/ANY breaches (zero survivors always pass). apply_cardinality truncates to one row for FIRST/PRIORITY/ANY.

concepts.name: Batch evaluation internals
concepts.description: evaluate_batch() conforms contexts to the rules frame's backend before cross-joining (_conform_to_rules_backend), then ranks per __context_id portably without window functions. Opt-in chunked evaluation exists with cross-chunk violation accumulation for hit-policy assertions over large batches.

concepts.name: Accumulator build algorithm
concepts.description: The build phase assigns unique primes to rules, creates an anchor lattice from single-rule entries, then iteratively expands by cross-joining compatible rules and coalescing their dimension values. A frontier filter removes dominated combinations (those whose prime product divides a larger combination's product). Each level is materialised via relation(...).collect() -- never re-chained lazily (exponential plan blow-up).

concepts.name: Ternary partition routing
concepts.description: New since the prior profile: LatticeIndex routes CONTEXT_KEY-partitioned contexts to the right lattice via ternary + specificity semantics using an embedded meta-engine over EXACT_KEY dimensions. An all-wildcard key is the default/overflow partition; exact hits keep an O(1) dict fast path; ties raise AmbiguousPartitionError (a KeyError subclass). index(lattices, validate=True) runs an exhaustive witness-matrix ambiguity check at load time.

concepts.name: Lattice persistence
concepts.description: New since the prior profile, which flagged 'no serialisation protocol' as an open question. Lattice.save/load round-trips a lattice through parquet + manifest.yaml, a superset of mountainash-rules-babel's LatticeManifest. Build offline, save, serve apply() from load.

concepts.name: Prime product identity and limits
concepts.description: Two independent bounds: combination width (~15 primes per combination, intrinsic to int64, enforced by checked_multiply/LatticeWidthExceededError) and rules-per-partition (MAX_RULES_PER_PARTITION=10,000, the prime table size, an explicit policy constant -- much larger than the prior profile's ~500-rule estimate). Exceeding the partition cap raises from get_prime; remediate with a CONTEXT_KEY dimension.

concepts.name: Backend purity enforcement
concepts.description: No module under src/mountainash_rules/ may import polars/ibis/narwhals directly -- only mountainash.relations/mountainash.expressions. tests/test_backend_purity.py enforces this package-wide, parametrised over every non-dunder module with no exemptions. Exactly three documented '# allow:' escapes exist: the per-row REGEX fallback (core/compiler.py), the empty-build schema seed (engines/accumulator/engine.py), and the snapshot parquet read (engines/accumulator/lattice.py) -- each pending a specific upstream mountainash capability.

concepts.name: Test suite structure
concepts.description: The test tree now mirrors the src/ package layout one-to-one (tests/core/, tests/filter/, tests/accumulator/, tests/benchmarks/) plus package-wide tests/test_backend_purity.py and tests/test_public_api.py. CI runs pytest+coverage, ruff, and radon on PRs; known upstream issues are xfailed via tests/conftest.py's _UPSTREAM_XFAILS.
